title: Vos tenés: regional variation
summary: Recognise and understand voseo, ustedes for everyone, seseo and yeísmo, Latin American words and tense preferences.
content:
## Vos: voseo

In Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and much of Central America, **vos** replaces **tú**. The present stresses the ending and has no stem change:

| tú | vos |
|---|---|
| eres | **sos** |
| hablas | **hablás** |
| tienes | **tenés** |
| quieres | **querés** |
| puedes | **podés** |
| ven, di (imperative) | **vení**, **decí** |

The pronoun **te** and the possessive **tu** stay: *¿Cómo **te** llamás **vos**?*

## Ustedes for all of you

In Latin America and the Canary Islands, **ustedes** is the only plural 'you', friendly or formal, with the third-person plural verb: *Chicos, ¿**ustedes vienen** a la fiesta?* (Spain: *¿vosotros venís?*). Vosotros forms are understood but not used.

## Sounds: seseo and yeísmo

- **distinción** (most of Spain): *casa* (s) and *caza* (th) sound different.
- **seseo** (Latin America, the Canaries, much of Andalusia): **ce, ci, z** sound like **s**, so *casa* and *caza* sound the same. **ceceo** (parts of Andalusia) does the opposite.
- **yeísmo** (almost everywhere): **ll** and **y** sound the same: *pollo / poyo*. In the River Plate both sound like English 'sh' or 's' in 'measure'.

## Words and tenses

| Spain | much of Latin America |
|---|---|
| el coche | el carro, el auto |
| el ordenador | la computadora |
| el móvil | el celular |
| el zumo | el jugo |
| las gafas | los anteojos, los lentes |
| el piso | el departamento, el apartamento |
| conducir | manejar |

For today, Spain says *hoy **he comido***; most of Latin America *hoy **comí***. **Ahorita** (Mexico) means 'right now' or 'in a little while'. Every variety is standard in its own region.

vocabulary.meaning: you (informal singular, River Plate and Central America)
vocabulary.example: ¿Y vos qué pensás de todo esto?
vocabulary.example_meaning: And what do you think about all this?

vocabulary.example: Vos sos la persona más paciente que conozco.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You're the most patient person I know.

vocabulary.example: ¿Vos tenés hora? Se me murió el celular.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Have you got the time? My phone died.

vocabulary.example: Vení, que te presento a mis amigos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Come here, I'll introduce you to my friends.

vocabulary.meaning: you all (formal and informal in Latin America and the Canaries)
vocabulary.example: ¿Ustedes ya cenaron, chicos?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Have you guys had dinner yet?

vocabulary.meaning: pronouncing ce, ci and z as s
vocabulary.example: El seseo es la norma en toda Latinoamérica.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Seseo is the norm throughout Latin America.

vocabulary.meaning: pronouncing s and z/ce/ci differently (most of Spain)
vocabulary.example: Con la distinción, casa y caza suenan distinto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: With distinción, casa and caza sound different.

vocabulary.meaning: pronouncing ll and y the same
vocabulary.example: Por el yeísmo, muchos niños escriben cabayo en vez de caballo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Because of yeísmo, many children write cabayo instead of caballo.

vocabulary.example: Dejé el carro en el estacionamiento del centro comercial.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I left the car in the shopping centre car park.

vocabulary.example: Se me trabó la computadora en plena reunión.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My computer froze in the middle of the meeting.

vocabulary.example: Mandame un mensaje al celular cuando llegues.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Send me a message on my phone when you get there.

vocabulary.example: Para desayunar, un jugo de naranja y unas tostadas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: For breakfast, an orange juice and some toast.

vocabulary.example: Aprendí a manejar a los dieciocho años.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I learnt to drive at eighteen.

vocabulary.meaning: right now; in a little while (Mexico and elsewhere)
vocabulary.example: Ahorita no puedo, pero en un rato te llamo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I can't right now, but I'll call you in a bit.

quiz.explanation: The voseo form of ser is sos.
hints: Vos has its own form of ser.

quiz.explanation: In the voseo present the stress falls on the ending and the stem does not change: tenés.
hints: No -ie-, accent on the last syllable.

quiz.explanation: The voseo imperative drops the -r of the infinitive and stresses the end: venir → vení.

quiz.prompt: A teacher in Mexico to her class: «¿___ ya terminaron el examen?»
quiz.explanation: In Latin America ustedes is the plural 'you' in every register; the verb (terminaron) is third-person plural.

quiz.prompt: In Madrid, to two friends: «¿Vosotros ___ (venir) a la fiesta?»
quiz.explanation: In Spain the informal plural is vosotros: venís.

quiz.prompt: A speaker who pronounces casa and caza exactly the same has…
quiz.explanation: Seseo: z, ce and ci sound like s.

quiz.prompt: In Mexico, what Spaniards call el móvil is usually…
quiz.explanation: El celular is the mobile phone in most of Latin America.

quiz.prompt: In much of Latin America: «Hoy ___ (comer, yo) temprano.» (simple past)
quiz.explanation: Most of Latin America uses the preterite even for today; Spain would say he comido.

quiz.prompt: True or false: voseo, seseo and ustedes for everyone are standard Spanish in the regions where they are used.
quiz.explanation: Voseo, seseo, ustedes for everyone and Spain's distinción are all standard Spanish in their regions.
hints: Think of how many countries speak Spanish.

listening.meaning: You're from Rosario, aren't you?
Would you all like something to drink?
I'll be right back, don't go.
I bought myself a new mobile.

listening.text: En Canarias se dice guagua en vez de autobús.
listening.meaning: In the Canaries they say guagua instead of autobús.
listening.note: New word: la guagua = the bus (Canaries and Caribbean).

listening.text: Alquilamos un departamento cerca del centro.
listening.meaning: We rented a flat near the centre.
listening.note: New word: el departamento = the flat (Latin America).

listening.text: Mañana te llamo desde la computadora de la oficina.
listening.meaning: Tomorrow I'll call you from the office computer.

listening.text: Si querés, vení a cenar el sábado con tu hermana.
listening.meaning: If you like, come for dinner on Saturday with your sister.

guide.tip: You don't have to speak every variety, but you should understand them all, because hundreds of millions of people speak them.

conversations.title: Two accents
conversations.scenario: Martina, from Buenos Aires, and Pablo, from Madrid, meet at a language exchange in Valencia.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Are you from here, from Valencia?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No, soy de Madrid. ¿Y tú? Por el acento, de Argentina.
lines.meaning: No, I'm from Madrid. And you? From the accent, Argentina.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, de Buenos Aires. Ustedes hablan muy rápido, eh.
lines.meaning: Yes, from Buenos Aires. You lot talk really fast, you know.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Us? You do too. Well, you all.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ayer pedí un jugo y el camarero me miró raro.
lines.meaning: Yesterday I asked for a jugo and the waiter gave me a funny look.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Aquí decimos zumo. Pero te entendió, seguro.
lines.meaning: Here we say zumo. But he understood you, for sure.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Y cuando dije que iba a manejar, pensaron que iba a trabajar con las manos.
lines.meaning: And when I said I was going to drive, they thought I'd be working with my hands.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ja, ja. Aquí es conducir. ¿Vos tenés carro? Así se dice, ¿no?
lines.meaning: Ha ha. Here it's conducir. Have you got a car? That's how you say it, right?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: En Argentina decimos auto. Carro dicen en México y Colombia.
lines.meaning: In Argentina we say auto. Carro is what they say in Mexico and Colombia.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues ven conmigo, que te enseño el mejor bar de zumos de la ciudad.
lines.meaning: Well, come with me and I'll show you the best juice bar in the city.

bites.title: Vos sos, vos tenés
bites.rule: Voseo: vos sos, tenés, querés, podés (stress on the end, no stem change). Imperative: vení, decí, hablá. Te and tu stay.

bites.title: Ustedes for everyone
bites.rule: In Latin America and the Canaries, ustedes is every plural 'you', with the ellos verb form: ustedes vienen.

bites.title: Seseo, yeísmo
bites.rule: Seseo: z, ce, ci sound like s (casa = caza). Yeísmo: ll = y (pollo = poyo). Spain's distinción keeps s and z apart.
bites.example: Cocinar suena como cosinar con seseo.

bites.title: Carro, celular, jugo
bites.rule: Coche/carro, ordenador/computadora, móvil/celular, zumo/jugo, conducir/manejar. Spain: hoy he comido; Latin America: hoy comí.

sorts.title: Usual in Spain or in most of Latin America?
sorts.why: Same things, different everyday words; all are understood everywhere.

sorts.title: Tú or vos?
sorts.why: Vos forms stress the ending and keep the stem unchanged.

spots.sentence: Vos eres muy simpático y tenés razón.
spots.why: The voseo form of ser is sos, like tenés.

spots.sentence: Vos tienes razón y sos muy listo.
spots.why: Voseo: tenés, without the stem change.

spots.sentence: En México, ustedes sois muy amables.
spots.why: Ustedes takes the third-person plural: son.
With vos the pronoun stays te.

builds.meaning: Are you all coming to the party?
I'll call you in a moment.

realm.content:
## Las variedades de Eldmark

Travel through Eldmark and you'll hear every kind of Spanish. The river elves of the south say **vos sos** and **vení**, the dwarves of Deepanvil call everyone **ustedes**, and in Highgate they keep **vosotros**. Ask for **jugo** or **zumo** of blackberry, and the innkeeper understands both.

vocabulary.example: Vos sos el mejor arquero del sur.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You're the best archer in the south.

vocabulary.example: Vení, que el río está tranquilo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Come on, the river is calm.

vocabulary.example: ¿Ustedes también van a Frostmarch, aventureros?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Are you heading to Frostmarch too, adventurers?

vocabulary.example: Un jugo de moras para la elfa, por favor.
vocabulary.example_meaning: A blackberry juice for the elf, please.

vocabulary.example: Vos tenés el arco más bonito del reino.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You've got the finest bow in the kingdom.

vocabulary.example: Por su acento, la elfa es del sur.
vocabulary.example_meaning: From her accent, the elf is from the south.

vocabulary.example: Los viajeros traen palabras nuevas a Highgate.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Travellers bring new words to Highgate.

vocabulary.example: Los enanos tienen un dialecto lleno de palabras de piedra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarves have a dialect full of stone words.

bites.title: Un reino, muchas voces
bites.rule: Eldmark has the same varieties as Earth. You hear vos sos in the south, ustedes among the dwarves and vosotros in Highgate. All of them are correct.
bites.example_meaning: You're from the south, aren't you?

listening.meaning: You're from the south, aren't you?
She has a southern accent.
listening.note: New word: el acento = the accent.

listening.meaning: Are you all going to Frostmarch too?
Travellers bring new words.
listening.note: New word: el viajero = the traveller.

listening.meaning: The dwarves speak another dialect.
listening.note: New word: el dialecto = the dialect.

spots.sentence: Vos eres el mejor arquero del sur y lo sabés.

spots.why: Ustedes takes the third-person pronoun and verb: se van.

sorts.title: ¿Quién lo diría?

items.text: Vení, que el río está tranquilo.
Vos tenés el arco más bonito.

sorts.why: Vos, ustedes and vosotros each have their own verb forms.

quiz.prompt: The southern elf says: «Vos ___ el mejor arquero del sur.»
Por su ___, la elfa es del sur.

meadowbrook.content:
## Las variedades en Meadowbrook

Leo's cousin Tomás arrives by boat from across the sea and the whole town listens: ***vos tenés** unas fresas preciosas*, he tells Nora; he asks Rosa for a **jugo**, calls his phone **el celular** and promises everything **ahorita**. At the pier, Leo translates, though nobody really needs him to.

vocabulary.example: Vos tenés unas fresas preciosas, Nora.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You've got lovely strawberries, Nora.

vocabulary.example: Rosa, ¿me das un jugo de fresa?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa, can I have a strawberry juice?

vocabulary.example: Tomás saca fotos de las vacas con el celular.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tomás takes photos of the cows with his phone.

vocabulary.example: Ahorita te ayudo con la cosecha.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'll help you with the harvest in a moment.

vocabulary.example: Vení, Nora, que te enseño mi barca.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Come here, Nora, I'll show you my boat.

vocabulary.example: La barca de Tomás llegó al muelle al amanecer.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tomás's boat reached the pier at dawn.

vocabulary.example: En su puerto todos hablan de vos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In his port everyone uses vos.

vocabulary.example: Tomás y Leo bajan el río en canoa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tomás and Leo go down the river by canoe.

bites.title: El primo del otro lado del mar
bites.rule: Tomás says vos tenés, jugo, celular and ahorita. Meadowbrook says tú tienes, zumo, móvil and ahora. Everybody understands everybody.

listening.text: Vos tenés una barca muy linda.
listening.meaning: You've got a really lovely boat.
The boat reached the pier.
listening.note: New word: el muelle = the pier.

listening.meaning: I'll help you in a moment.
We went down the river by canoe.
listening.note: New word: la canoa = the canoe.

listening.text: En el puerto de Tomás se habla de vos.
listening.meaning: In Tomás's port people use vos.
listening.note: New word: el puerto = the port.

builds.text: Ahorita te ayudo con la cosecha.
builds.meaning: I'll help you with the harvest in a moment.

spots.sentence: Vos tienes unas fresas preciosas y las vendés baratas.

spots.why: Voseo forms carry an accent on the last syllable.

quiz.prompt: Tomás to Nora: «Vos ___ (tener) unas fresas preciosas.»
hints: No stem change, accent on the end.

quiz.prompt: Tomás asks for un jugo. In Meadowbrook (Spain) they'd say…

rustwake.content:
## Las variedades en el páramo

Tune the wrist radio and other domes come through. One station says ***¿ustedes** me escuchan?*, another ***¿vos me escuchás?***, and ours says ***¿me escucháis?*** One announcer **sesea**, another doesn't. Each dome speaks a different Spanish, but the message is the same: *hay agua en la antena*.

vocabulary.example: ¿Ustedes me escuchan? Aquí la cúpula del norte.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Can you all hear me? This is the north Dome.

vocabulary.example: ¿Vos me escuchás, Leo?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Can you hear me, Leo?

vocabulary.example: La locutora del sur tiene seseo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The southern announcer has seseo.

vocabulary.example: Ahorita repetimos el mensaje.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We'll repeat the message in a moment.

vocabulary.example: ¿Vos tenés pilas para el radiorreloj?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Have you got batteries for the wrist radio?

vocabulary.example: Hay tres emisoras nuevas en el páramo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There are three new radio stations in the wasteland.

vocabulary.example: Cambia la frecuencia y escucha la otra cúpula.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Change the frequency and listen to the other Dome.

vocabulary.example: La transmisión llega con mucho ruido.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The broadcast comes through with a lot of noise.

bites.title: Otras cúpulas en la radio
bites.rule: On the radio: ¿ustedes me escuchan? (Latin American plural), ¿vos me escuchás? (voseo), ¿me escucháis? (vosotros). All mean the same.

listening.meaning: Do you all have filtered water?
Leo, have you got a signal?
There's a new radio station.
listening.note: New word: la emisora = the radio station.

listening.meaning: Change the frequency.
listening.note: New word: la frecuencia = the frequency.

listening.meaning: The broadcast comes through with noise.
listening.note: New word: la transmisión = the broadcast.

spots.why: Ustedes takes the third-person pronoun and verb: se quedan.

spots.sentence: ¿Vos me escuchas o seguís dormido, Leo?
spots.why: Voseo stresses the ending: escuchás, like seguís.

sorts.title: ¿Qué cúpula habla?
sorts.why: Each variety has its own verb forms for 'you'.

quiz.prompt: «Cambia la ___ y escucha la otra cúpula.»
quiz.explanation: You change the frequency to reach another station.
